officialName.note: Search-snippet lead (official domain, 2026-10-12) — NOT verified; read the official page before publishing. Snippets (search-tool summaries): official chmnu.edu.ua pages (Foreign Students, General information, Conditions and tuition fees, History) describe Petro Mohyla Black Sea National University. The Ukrainian name «Чорноморський національний університет імені Петра Могили» was seen only on a THIRD-PARTY site (cris.fau.de, paired with the English name); the abbreviation ЧНУ matches the strategic-plan file name 'Strategichnij_plan_CHNU_2025-2029.pdf' on the official domain. Other titles in use: "Petro Mohyla Black Sea State University" (Wikipedia, THIRD-PARTY) and "Black Sea National University named after Petro Mohyla" (SUCHO database, THIRD-PARTY). The university has a Medical Institute (Медичний інститут; one of four institutes per a search-tool summary), a unit of the university, not a separate university; a THIRD-PARTY mirror of 2024 state admissions data (vstup.osvita.ua) lists the Medicine programme there; its exact official English name is unconfirmed. Confirm the full official name, in English and Ukrainian, on the official homepage.

status.note: Search-snippet lead (official domain, 2026-10-12) — NOT verified; read the official page before publishing. Basis (adversarial re-check, 2026-10-12): dated official 2025 documents on chmnu.edu.ua — the foreigners' fee page cites an Academic Council decision (Minutes No. 11, 29 August 2025) and the domain hosts a 2025–2029 strategic plan — indicate the university was operating in 2025. No relocation, occupation, closure or merger lead appeared, and every source places it in Mykolaiv. THIRD-PARTY reports (pravda.com.ua, Kyiv Post, Ukrinform, August 2022; not re-checked): "As a result of five missiles hitting the buildings of the educational institution, the main building was heavily damaged"; computer classes, scientific laboratories and the University Clinic were also damaged. A DAAD Studybridge report (THIRD-PARTY, January 2024; its attribution to this university is not verified) says most courses were taught online. No official statement for 2025–26 or 2026–27 found.

statusStatement.note: No current-year official statement found: Ukrainian- and English-language searches returned no 2025 or 2026 statement on where or how teaching takes place (in person, blended or online) or on shelters. The latest lead is THIRD-PARTY and out of date: a DAAD Studybridge report (January 2024, attribution unverified) says "the uncertainty of the situation and location of the University close to the battlefront did not allow for 'regular' teaching, so most courses were taught online". A NikVesti article about Mykolaiv universities in general (THIRD-PARTY, date uncertain, content likely 2023) says students had been studying online for a year. Quote the current official statement verbatim with its date.

overview: Research draft record, unpublished: every statement below is an unverified lead, not a verified fact. A multidisciplinary university in Mykolaiv, Ukraine, with a Medical Institute (a unit of the university, not a separate university); according to a search-tool snippet, its official fee page for foreigners (fees approved by the Academic Council in August 2025) lists a six-year Master's in Medicine, but the Medicine fee itself was not shown. Draft record built from search-snippet leads on 2026-10-12. Mykolaiv is war-affected: third-party reports say the main building was heavily damaged by missiles in August 2022, and no dated official statement on teaching format for 2025–26 or 2026–27 was found, so whether, where and how foreign students are taught in 2026–27 is an open question. No fee, deadline or intake date is recorded. Every field below is awaiting verification against the official pages listed under research references and nothing here is presented as a current fact.

accreditation.note: Record accreditation only from a NAQA register entry or the official certificate. Nothing recorded. Kept strictly separate: (1) State registration (EDEBO): no EDEBO register entry seen (an access limitation, not evidence); the Ministry "Study in Ukraine" portal contacts page (entry ID 13, paraphrase) gives state ownership — a portal listing, not a register record. (2) Licence: no MON licence record or EDEBO licence record seen, for the university or for specialty 222 Medicine. The official International activities page (undated, search-tool summary) says "The university has a license to train foreign students" — the university's own claim, with no date and no licence number; it is not a register record and names no programme licence. (3) National programme accreditation (NAQA): a NAQA decision hosted on the university domain (file '222_Rishennya_Natsionalnogo_agentstva.pdf', dated 26 December 2023, protocol No. 21 (50); search-tool summary) cites the procedure for accrediting educational programmes and says the agency decided to accredit a programme; the snippet cuts off before naming the programme, the accreditation type and the term, so it is NOT confirmed to cover Medicine (222) — only the file name suggests specialty 222 — and it was not re-checked; no NAQA register entry found. (4) International accreditation (for example by a WFME-aligned agency): none found. (5) A THIRD-PARTY database (which result said this is not identified; possibly uni2study or SUCHO) lists the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine as the 'accrediting agency' — generic, not a licence, accreditation or register record. A 2021 official brochure listing Medicine under specialty 222 is a programme description, not a licence or accreditation statement.

recognition.note: Recognition is decided separately by each destination country's regulator (for example India's National Medical Commission). Record it only from a tier-4 page on a recognition-authority host the owner has listed (N24 b; none listed yet), quoting what that page says, with its date. A World Directory of Medical Schools (WDOMS) listing is a directory entry, not recognition; a university's own claim of WHO, NMC or ECFMG recognition is not recognition; an international accreditation is not recognition; institutional registration (EDEBO), programme licence and programme accreditation (NAQA) are separate claims. Claims seen, none recorded: the official General information page (search-tool paraphrase) says the university is a member of the European University Association (EUA), the Magna Charta Universitatum (MCU), the World Health Organization (WHO) and the Medical Council of India; a search-tool summary says the Ministry "Study in Ukraine" portal describes it as "accredited/recognised by the Ministry of Health of Ukraine, Medical Council of India(MCI) and World Health Organisation (WHO)". Both are the university's or the portal's own wording, not a decision by a destination-country regulator and not a WDOMS entry; no WDOMS check was performed. Never imply a right to practise in any country.
